hook: This entry is almost entirely pictures: stick figures, arrows and symbols, with barely any ordinary prose. That isn't a gimmick for its own sake. Read it slowly, panel by panel, and ask yourself why a containment file would be written this way before the drawings tell you.
whyItMatters: Its rating puts it near the very top of the site, which is remarkable for a page you can finish in under a minute. It proved that an SCP article can communicate through form alone, and it is the obvious example whenever people talk about experimental formats on the wiki. Even the title is part of the design: the groups of dots spell out the item number without a single digit.
thingsToNotice: The premise flips the usual relationship between a document and its anomaly. Normally the file is how the Foundation keeps control; here, plain written description is exactly what puts things at risk, so the drawing-only format is itself the containment procedure. Notice how much the pictures convey without words, such as threat, location and consequence, and how much they leave for you to infer. By the end you may realize that you, the reader, are standing inside the rule as well.

related.note: Another anomaly that defeats its own paperwork, this time by refusing to be remembered.
A lighter case of an object that changes how people are able to talk about it.
